items.academicConcern: The source asks for crystalline, polycrystalline and amorphous solids; correct explanations distinguish long-range ordered crystals, multiple crystalline grains/grain boundaries and disordered materials. The official B-22 summative SLO also names glassy and polymeric structures, so this original response alone is not comprehensive evidence of the full SLO.
items.proposedTeacherTreatment: Preserve original as a valid comparison. Add short examples and acknowledge that polymers may be partly crystalline or amorphous and glassy state is another descriptor. Assess named B-22 categories elsewhere.

items.academicConcern: The source chapter gives three cubic cell centerings (SC, BCC, FCC) on printed p115 and seven crystal systems based on lengths/angles on printed p116. 'Types' is underspecified if the model answer confuses these taxonomies. Neither should be silently presented as the only possible classification.
items.proposedTeacherTreatment: Retain original textbook question. Provide two separately labelled tables or diagrams in the teacher rubric, and identify cubic cell-centering separately from seven crystal systems. Note the named B-22 SLO covers distinguishing solid structures rather than requiring every lattice derivation.

items.academicConcern: Stress is force per relevant area and axial strain is fractional change in length; Young's modulus is tensile stress divided by tensile strain in the proportional region. 'Modulus of elasticity' can also name a broader family of moduli; the source focus is Young's modulus. Defining terms is Understanding, whereas official B-24 is Application.
items.proposedTeacherTreatment: Keep original as foundational theory. Scope the marking scheme explicitly to Young's modulus and units while teaching the generic term carefully; add a distinct applied calculation if using this response to certify B-24 Application.

items.academicConcern: A defensible ductile stress–strain diagram must label stress on the vertical axis and strain horizontally; distinguish proportional limit, elastic limit/yield, plastic deformation, ultimate tensile strength and fracture. Do not equate proportional limit with elastic limit.
items.proposedTeacherTreatment: Retain the original long question; mark a teacher-approved, accessible originally drawn schematic with correct axis labels and the main regions. Check that source Figure7.12's schematic labels are explained without universalizing their exact locations to all alloys.

items.academicConcern: Elastic deformation can remain recoverable beyond the strictly proportional (Hookean) range; plastic deformation leaves permanent strain after unloading. A source curve with plastic and elastic regions must not label every nonlinear segment as plastic. This original question substantially overlaps Q7.4.
items.proposedTeacherTreatment: Keep original for separate teaching. Require correct proportional-vs-elastic/yield boundary and residual deformation in a teacher rubric; rotate Q7.4/Q7.5 in a short summative paper rather than double-counting identical diagram content.

items.academicConcern: Work done by a variable tensile force is the integral of force with respect to extension. The source NBF Figure7.14 (printed p122) plots weight horizontally and extension vertically; its 'area under curve' claim is not generally valid for that orientation. The correct area-work graph has extension horizontally and force vertically.
items.proposedTeacherTreatment: Retain the original and its justified physics. In a source-linked scored long response require W=integral F dx and an accessible, correctly oriented teacher-drawn force-versus-extension graph; for a linear ramp from zero show the triangular half-F-x area.

items.academicConcern: A full energy derivation must start from zero-to-final linear elastic loading: W=integral_0^x F(s) ds with F=kx. Under this proportional assumption U=half k x^2=half F x=Y A x^2/(2L). For nonlinear response the general integral remains, and stress–strain area gives energy per unit volume rather than total joules.
items.proposedTeacherTreatment: Keep original. The approved response must state proportional-range assumptions, intermediate force/extension steps and energy units joules; distinguish total stored potential energy from strain-energy density J/m^3.

items.academicConcern: The text on NBF p122 describes reference and test metallic wires with a vernier readout and variable loading on the test wire. A complete reproducible experimental answer should identify both wires, initial length L, diameter or area A, incremental force F, extension x, and the relation Y=FL/(Ax), with readings in the proportional range. Simply quoting the formula is not a description of the experiment.
items.proposedTeacherTreatment: Keep original. Approve a correctly labelled original/permission-cleared two-wire vernier apparatus diagram or accessible stepwise explanation with measured quantities and loading range; do not publish a cropped textbook diagram to the public repository.
